$comment: The closed list of environment variables: everything else is settings in the settings table and the panel. A test finds any access to process.env.X (and readEnv("X")) in packages/*/src, except packages/mocks, and requires an entry here with that package in packages.
A new variable is an exception: it needs an entry here with a reason in English.
packages — packages where access is allowed (the directory name in packages/); why — why the variable exists if everything else is in the panel.
Variables of the install path (MEMORY_DEPLOY_PROFILE and others) follow the same rule.

PORT.why: port of the process listener: process layout, needed before the database is read

PG_HOST.why: PostgreSQL address: without it there is no settings table

PG_PORT.why: PostgreSQL port: without it there is no settings table

PGSSLMODE.why: shared: TLS mode of the PostgreSQL connections (libpq's word); read once by pg-tls.ts

PGSSLROOTCERT.why: shared: file with the certificate authority of the PostgreSQL server; read once by pg-tls.ts

MEMORY_PG_TLS_NO_VERIFY.why: shared: the word "allow" permits PGSSLMODE=no-verify; without it that mode stops the start

PG_APP_PASSWORD.why: password of the application roles and the encryption key of the settings secrets: needed before the database is read

DB_PASS.why: not a memory variable: an example of accessing a field in the text of the open check rule (open-check.ts); the line is here so that the search does not confuse the example with a read

MEMORY_INSTANCE_ID.why: which instance to read from the settings table

MEMORY_ROLE.why: role of the process (gateway or worker): which database pools to open and the name in the log

MEMORY_DEPLOY_PROFILE.why: deploy profile — internet, internal-http or development: which start rules apply (install code, listeners, internal networks); needed before the database is read; unset means internet, an unknown value stops the start

MEMORY_SECRETS_MODE.why: secrets mode — files (per-service secret files, the default) or legacy-derived (role passwords and keys may still be derived from PG_APP_PASSWORD): decides which secrets the process may start with, before the database and the settings table are reachable; PG_APP_PASSWORD without legacy-derived and an unknown value stop the start

MEMORY_PUBLIC_URL.why: public address of the installation (an https origin behind the reverse proxy): its host joins the external host list and it is the fallback of the agents' address; it must match the proxy the compose file starts and work before the first administrator exists, so it is not a panel setting; nothing is written to the database; in admin: public https address of the install: session cookies of the workplace and panel get Secure even when the TLS proxy does not send X-Forwarded-Proto; set by the deployment

MEMORY_TRUSTED_PROXIES.why: CIDR list of the reverse proxies as the gateway sees them, added to access.trusted_proxies: the client address and the request channel depend on it before any administrator can change settings (on a basic install without an identity provider the panel cannot change trusted proxies at all); nothing is written to the database

MEMORY_TEST_HOOKS.why: test hooks of a test installation; never set in production

VITEST.why: set by the vitest runner, never by a person or a deployment: the test-only switches of the locale scope and of the fallback time zone refuse to work without it

MEMORY_LOG_LEVEL.why: log verbosity before the database is read

MEMORY_COMMIT.why: build version for /api/v1/health; set by the build

MEMORY_CONTRACTS_DIR.why: where the contracts are in the image; in connectors: the connector SDK finds contracts/connectors the way shared finds the contracts, without importing shared (connectors test/imports.test.ts keeps the SDK off @memory/shared)

MEMORY_FIRST_RUN_CODE.why: one-time code of the first run (creating the first administrator), until an administrator exists

MEMORY_LLM_STUB.why: model stub of a test installation; never set in production

MEMORY_LLM_REQUIRE_FLOOR.why: require the model request arbiter (the “no more than one request at a time” rule)

MEMORY_LLM_TURN.why: flag that probe tools are launched through the queue to the model

GATEWAY_URL.why: gateway address for the panel: the panel does not read the settings table

MEMORY_DISK_GUARD_PATHS.why: stop of file intake by location: which directories on the file systems of the database data and the storage are mounted into the gateway read-only (empty marker directories, not the data itself) — the volume layout known to the deployment, not to the administrator; empty — health warns “location stop is not configured”; an entry that is not “/” closes intake

MEMORY_SCRYPT_PARALLEL.why: the number of scrypt runs of local accounts at once, 1 or 2 (unset means 2), read once at start by local-accounts.ts; the start refuses a number whose memory does not fit the cgroup limit of the gateway

CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY.why: set by systemd (LoadCredential), not by a person: the service secrets directory and the run mode marker

RUNTIME_DIRECTORY.why: set by systemd, not by a person: the directory of the service sockets and temporary files

XDG_RUNTIME_DIR.why: set by systemd for user units, not by a person

NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS.why: Node’s trust in the company root certificate is needed before the database is read

HTTPS_PORT.why: port of the panel HTTPS: the panel does not read the settings table (the gateway has the setting access.https_port)

MEMORY_ADMIN_LISTEN.why: address of the admin plane listener: process layout, like PORT

MEMORY_WORKPLACE_LISTEN.why: address of the workspace listener: process layout

MEMORY_CLI_LISTEN.why: address of the administrator command-line listener: process layout

MEMORY_CLI_SOCKET.why: path of the administrator command-line socket: process layout

MEMORY_WEB_ROLE.why: which of the two panel builds is running (admin plane or workspace)

GATEWAY_ADMIN_URL.why: address of the gateway admin listener for the panel: the panel does not read the settings table

NODE_ENV.why: set by Next.js, not by a person: next start — production, next dev — development; the panel uses it to decide Secure on the memory_panel cookie

NEXT_RUNTIME.why: set by Next.js itself (nodejs | edge), not a setting: instrumentation.ts reads the installation values only in the Node runtime

MEMORY_ANCHORS_DIR.why: where the signed anchors are kept: they must survive a takeover of the panel

MEMORY_EXPORT_DIR.why: the only directory the whole-instance export job may write to: a deployment mount, not a panel setting, so that a panel administrator cannot redirect closed data

MEMORY_RELEASE_UPLOAD.why: release through activation by a person is on: the “Readiness” check for advanced only reads the flag, the deployment decides
